articles.title: KingCobra 1.0: a native systems language that feels like a scripting language
articles.excerpt: I'm Divyanshu, I'm 17, and I've spent a long time building KingCobra, a programming language that tries to feel like a scripting language while behaving like a systems language. v1.0.0 is out now, and…
articles.body: I'm Divyanshu, I'm 17, and I've spent a long time building KingCobra , a programming language that tries to feel like a scripting language while behaving like a systems language. v1.0.0 is out now , and on Windows it installs with a single choco install kingcobra . let nums = [5, 3, 8, 1, 9]; let [first, ...rest] = nums; print(nums.map(fn(x) -> int { return x * x; }).filter(fn(x) -> bool { return x > 10; })); What is it? KingCobra has a small, readable syntax and a REPL: let / var , f-strings, slicing, destructuring, match , structs and impl , enums, try / catch . Underneath, it gives you things scripting languages usually hide: explicit memory, C-style pointers, a real FFI and raw machine code.
articles.author: Divyanshu Sinha

Any answer to how many websites use React depends on what a scanner can observe in a React site, and that is worth understanding if you write or maintain React code. The live number sits on webatla's React technology page . The history tables and the full framework comparison are in the React statistics article on the webatla blog. What a scanner can and cannot see in a React build React renders in the browser and, in many setups, on the server as well. Either way the browser receives HTML plus JavaScript files, and React's client code takes over the page once they load.

articles.excerpt: NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Sp…
articles.body: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 24 mission launched Saturday, April 11, 2026, aboard the company’s Cygnus XL spacecraft atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: Northrop Grumman NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23.

articles.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
articles.excerpt: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its stellar companion.
articles.body: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean.
